carbon_policy_signal.item: EU Commission extends industry free pollution allowances to 2040s; loosens carbon market scarcity narrative and fuel-switch incentives.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Weaker EUA scarcity reduces gas-vs-coal merit-order spread; compressed clean-dark margin lowers power-plant fuel-switch call on thermal dispatch.

freshness_caveat: Coal data stale (208 days old, as of 2025-12-26); Clean Dark stale (203 days old, as of 2025-12-31). Current coal price (96 USD/t, 7th-percentile) and clean-dark spread (27.95 EUR/MWh, 48th-percentile) used for trend, but intraday moves unreliable. TTF, GB Power, DE Power, EUA, renewables, and storage current as of 2026-07-21/22.
risk_flags: Storage at 54.2% (28th-percentile, −15.5pp vs 5-yr seasonal) — refill pace critical for H2 power and gas curve shape through October.
GB power at 149.93 EUR/MWh (99th-percentile) — premium may reflect Irish wind forecast or interconnector constraint; watch for mean reversion if renewables recover.
TTF at 59.66 (73rd-percentile, +2.6σ above 50d trend) — Hormuz risk priced in; LNG supply growth (56.3 Bcf/d record) and weakening EU carbon narrative create downside tail to Cal+1.
EU carbon loosening extends free allocations to 2040s — fuel-switch margin compressed; coal (96 USD/t, 7th-percentile) signals weak merit-order call despite gas premium.

base.summary: Hormuz premium persists; storage refill steady; EU carbon policy drift. TTF holds 58–61 range; DE power 150–160.

downside.summary: Hormuz de-escalation, Middle East tension eases; record LNG supply quenches arb; EU carbon loosening cements bearish fuel-switch.

upside.summary: Hormuz escalation or Strait closing signal; LNG arb widens; storage refill stalls. TTF spike on supply scarcity.

themes: Geopolitical gas premium (Hormuz, Iran risk) offsetting record LNG supply
GB power spike vs EU storage 15.5pp-below-seasonal tightens winter demand
EU carbon policy loosening weakens fuel-switch incentives; coal collapsing (7th-percentile)
Clean spark elevated (84th-percentile); clean dark stable (48th-percentile)
top_drivers: Hormuz geopolitical premium locked into TTF (+2.6σ above 50d trend); Asian LNG demand and risk-off posture sustain bid.
EU storage deficit (−15.5pp below seasonal) tightens Cal+1 and winter curve; refill pace will determine Sept–Oct power premium.
EU carbon loosening (2040s allowance extension) weakens fuel-switch narrative; coal at 7th-percentile signals compressed dark-spread merit order despite gas premium.
Record global LNG (56.3 Bcf/d) and US capacity ramp offer downside tail to TTF if Hormuz risk re-prices lower or winter demand softens.
top_takeaway: GB power at 99th-percentile amid Hormuz premium and storage deficit; TTF extended 2.6σ on geopolitical tail-risk, but EU carbon loosening and record LNG supply offer downside anchor.

watchlist.metric: Strait of Hormuz traffic vs baseline
watchlist.why: Disruption would lift TTF +8–15% and tighten Q3–Q4 LNG arb; currently priced at risk-premium but not crisis-level.

watchlist.metric: EU carbon Parliament/member-state vote on 2040s allowance extension
watchlist.why: Bearish-EUA outcome likely; weakens fuel-switch thesis and cuts power-dispatch upside from clean spark (currently 84th-percentile).

watchlist.metric: EU storage refill pace and seasonal catch-up
watchlist.why: At 54.2% (−15.5pp), shortfall of ~5–7 TWh vs norm; slow refill locks in elevated Cal+1 and winter premium through September.
September deadline adds Q4 geopolitical drag; failure extends infrastructure uncertainty into heating season.

watchlist.metric: EU methane enforcement timeline and supplier response
watchlist.why: If compliance forces exits, TTF supply shock; low probability but high impact to Cal+1 and 2027 forwards.

watchlist.metric: US LNG export growth tracking record 56.3 Bcf/d
watchlist.why: Sustained growth dampens LNG-to-TTF arb; bearish for winter Cal+1 if Asian demand softens or supply outpaces demand.

watchlist_dated.name: NATO fuel pipeline Turkey compromise deadline
watchlist_dated.why: Infrastructure delay extends geopolitical uncertainty into Q4 heating-season gas demand curve.
